info.title: OpenAsy Live Chat API
info.summary: A chat window on your site from one script tag, answered by your team in the browser, with the visitor's pages from Analytics.
info.description:
Every screen of Live Chat uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

The window on a site's pages loads `/w/<site>.js` and talks to `/api/v1/widget/*` from pages of the site's hosts (CORS), with the chat's token once a chat starts. Sites, hours, teams, routing rules, the window's look and the links to Helpdesk, Analytics, CRM and Knowledge Base come from the settings file, never the API. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Both the team's screens and the window follow chats with Server-Sent Events whose ids are the events' sequence numbers, and resume after them.

CRM is sent leads with `POST <crm.url>/api/v1/leads`; the request and the answer are described here as `CrmLeadRequest` and `CrmLeadCreated`.

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.

get.summary: Settings, as the file sets them
get.description: There is no route that changes them: the settings file is the only way in. Needs the viewer role.

get.summary: The links to Helpdesk, Analytics, CRM and Knowledge Base
get.description: Whether each is linked, its secret is set, and when it last worked or failed. Needs the viewer role.
Members who answer chats, their teams, open chats, and whether they are available. Needs the viewer role.

put.description: Away members are not counted as available, so the window says an answer may take longer. Needs the editor role.

get.description: Chats today, the first answer, chats that became tickets or leads, chats per hour against the same day last week, the pages they started on, and the team now. Needs the viewer role.
Chats by page and by hour, the time to the first answer, and chats that became tickets or leads, overall and by team. Needs the viewer role.
Open chats: the oldest unanswered first. Closed: the newest first. Needs the viewer role.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A name, an email, a page, a number, or words said.

get.description: With everything said, the pages the window saw, suggested articles and the team's saved answers. Needs the viewer role.
Their visit from Analytics, when it is linked and the window sent its ids: where they came from and the pages they read. Needs the viewer role.

post.description: The first member to answer takes the chat. With client_id, sending the same line again answers 200 with the one added before. Needs the editor role.

200.description: The same client_id again: the line added before, not added twice.

post.description: The body is the file itself, with its type as content-type, its name in x-file-name (URI-encoded) and an optional x-client-id. Only the types and size in files are taken, and only when the bytes are that type. Needs the editor role.

200.description: The same client_id again: the line added before, not added twice.

post.description: To a member, another team, or both, with everything said so far. The visitor is told who answers now; the note stays with the team. Needs the editor role.
With the whole chat; what is said afterwards goes to the ticket too. When Helpdesk cannot be reached, ticket.error says why and it is tried again. Needs the editor role.
With the chat, the pages read and the agent as its owner (CrmLeadRequest). Only when crm is linked. Needs the editor role.

get.description: Each becomes a Helpdesk ticket. Needs the viewer role.
Plain images are shown inline; anything else is downloaded, in a sandbox. Needs the viewer role.

Server-Sent Events: `line` and `chat` events, each with `id:` its sequence number. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID (EventSource does) or ?after= to get what was missed, once. `event: reset` means the client is too far behind: load the chats again. Members who answer chats count as available while it is open. Needs the viewer role.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The sequence number of the last event seen; Last-Event-ID wins when both are sent. Default 0.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Sent by EventSource when it reconnects.

get.description: `<script src=".../w/<site>.js" defer></script>` on every page of the site. It carries the site's settings and may be cached for five minutes. On sites with consent, it waits for Consent's answer before it shows anything.

404.description: No such site; a comment that says so.

503.description: Not built; a comment that says so.

get.description: Whether the window offers a chat now, when it opens next, and how many are answering. Pages of the sites' hosts only (CORS); nothing about the visitor is sent or kept.
From Knowledge Base, before a chat starts. Nothing is kept.

post.description: Only in working hours (409 closed outside them). The page's rule picks the team. Up to 6 a minute from one address.
It becomes a Helpdesk ticket, answered by email. Up to 5 a minute from one address and 5 an hour from one email.

get.description: Everything shown to the visitor, and the last event's number to stream from.

patch.description: An email lets a chat no one answered become a ticket answered by email.

post.description: With client_id, sending the same line again answers 200 with the one added before, so a retry after a dropped connection adds it once. Up to 40 a minute.

200.description: The same client_id again: the line added before, not added twice.

post.description: The body is the file itself, with its type as content-type, its name in x-file-name (URI-encoded) and x-client-id. Only the types and size in files are taken, and only when the bytes are that type. Up to 10 a minute.

200.description: The same client_id again: the line added before, not added twice.

get.description: By the signed link the window was given. Plain images are shown inline; anything else is downloaded, in a sandbox.

post.summary: The page the visitor is on

post.description: A chat that ends on a question no one answered becomes a Helpdesk ticket.

get.description: Server-Sent Events of the visitor's chat: `line` and `chat` events with `id:` their sequence number. Resume with ?after= or Last-Event-ID. Read it with fetch, so the token goes in a header. Up to 6 open at once for a chat.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The sequence number of the last event seen; Last-Event-ID wins when both are sent. Default 0.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Sent by EventSource when it reconnects.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Live Chat runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Live Chat origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings, API tokens (`oa_live-chat_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Live Chat is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

chatToken.description: The token POST /api/v1/widget/chats returned: one chat's, for the visitor's window.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

anyOf.description: The settings file and whether it is applied; null before it was first read.

state.description: Available: their Live Chat screen is open and they are not away.

seq.description: Its event's sequence number: lines are in this order.

event.description: System lines: started, joined, handed, closed, ticket, ticket-asked, lead, ask-email or articles.

shown.description: Whether the visitor's window shows it.

clientId.description: The sender's own id for the line: the same id sent twice adds it once.

routedBy.description: The page rule that chose the team.

page.description: The path the chat started on.

pageNow.description: The path the visitor is on now.

waitingSince.description: Since when the visitor's last line has had no answer.

seq.description: The last event's sequence number when the list was read: open the stream after it.

routedBy.description: The page rule that chose the team.

page.description: The path the chat started on.

pageNow.description: The path the visitor is on now.

waitingSince.description: Since when the visitor's last line has had no answer.

answers.description: Saved answers for the chat's team, with the visitor's name filled in.

seq.description: The last event's sequence number: open the stream after it.

linked.description: Whether Analytics is linked for the chat's site.

ids.description: Whether the window sent Analytics' ids for this visit.

pages.description: The pages the window saw while the chat was open.

agent.description: A member's id; null takes the chat from whoever has it.

team.description: A team id from the settings file.

error.description: Why it is not a ticket yet; it is tried again.

secret.description: The environment variable the file names.

pending.description: Helpdesk: chats and questions waiting to become tickets.

firstAnswerTrend.description: The median of each of the last 14 days, in ms; 0 for days without answers.

slow.description: Chats today not answered within chats.slow_answer.

questions.description: Questions outside hours in the last 7 days.

byHour.description: Chats started, Monday first, by hour in the hours' time zone.

config.description: The applied settings, as the settings file sets them; null before it is applied.

name.description: The agent's name; null for the visitor's own lines.

url.description: Relative to Live Chat's address; signed, for this chat only.

email.description: Whether the visitor left an email.

page.description: The page's address, on one of the site's hosts. Only its path is kept.

referrer.description: document.referrer; only its host is kept.

analytics.description: openasy.ids() when Analytics' script is on the page.

token.description: The chat's secret: send it as Authorization: Bearer. Keep it in the site's own storage; nothing else identifies the visitor.

website.description: Leave empty: a hidden field that only bots fill.

external_id.description: live-chat-<chat id>: the same chat opens one lead.

page.description: The page the chat started on, as a full address.

title.description: The first question, up to 120 characters.

pages.description: The pages the visitor read, oldest first: from Analytics when linked, else from the window.

CrmLeadRequest.description: What Live Chat sends: POST <crm.url>/api/v1/leads with Authorization: Bearer <the token crm.token names>. Not served by Live Chat.

CrmLeadCreated.description: What CRM answers: 201 for a new lead, 200 for the one the same external_id opened before. Other fields are ignored.
